examples.text: [T]he ſhipmen deemed that they drew neere to ſome countrey: And ſounded, and found it twentie fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they ſounded againe, and found it fifteene fathoms.

Full fadom fiue thy Father lies,
Of his bones are Corrall made:
Those are pearles that were his eies,
Nothing of him that doth fade,

Into someting rich, & strange

glosses: A man's armspan, generally reckoned to be six feet (about 1.8 metres). Later used to measure the depth of water, but now generally replaced by the metre outside American usage.
An internationally standardized version of this unit, the international fathom (= 1.8288 metres = 6 feet).
A measure of distance to shore: the nearest point to shore at which the water depth is the value quoted.

examples.text: After we'd rowed for an hour, we found ourselves stranded ten fathoms from shore.
At fifty fathoms, the waters of the Southern Ocean are dark blue.

glosses: An unspecified depth.
Depth of insight; mental reach or scope.

examples.text: Another of his fathome they haue not / To leade their buſineſſe, […]

glosses: The act of stretching out one's arms away from the sides of the torso so that they make a straight line perpendicular to the body.
Someone or something that is embraced.

examples.text: Thy Bride, thy choice, thy vvife, / She that is novv thy fadom, […] Kneele at thy feete, obay in euerie thing, / So euerie Father is a priuate King.

glosses: Control, grasp.

examples.text: So; novv knovv I vvhere I am, me thinkes already / I graſpe beſt part of the Autumnian bleſſing / In my contentious fadome, […]
Yes: / you have blovvne his ſvvolne pride to that vaſtnes, / as he beleeves the earth is in his fadom, / this makes him qute forget his humble Being: […]

glosses: To measure the depth of (water); to take a sounding of; to sound.
To encircle (someone or something) with outstretched arms; specifically, to measure the circumference or (rare) length of something.
Often followed by out: to deeply understand (someone or something); to get to the bottom of.

examples.text: I can’t for the life of me fathom what this means.
Otamendi’s selection ahead of Vincent Kompany was difficult to fathom and, apart from Fernandinho, City’s line-up was otherwise filled with attacking players.

glosses: To embrace (someone or something).
To measure a depth; to sound.
To conduct an examination or inquiry; to investigate.

glosses: Healthy.

examples.text: He was safe and sound.
In horse management a sound horse is one with no health problems that might affect its suitability for its intended work.

on the 29th of September 1840, in consideration that the plaintiff, at the request of the defendant, had bought of the defendant a certain horse, at a certain price, to wit, 30l., the defendant promised plaintiff that the horse did not exceed five years off, and that it was sound in wind and limb, perfect in vision, and free from vice; […]

glosses: Complete, solid, or secure.

examples.text: Fred assured me the floorboards were sound.
The brasswork here, how rich it is in beams, / And how, besides, it makes the whole house sound.
Refurbishing Okehampton station, kept basically sound under ownership by Devon Council, remains a work in progress and scheduled for completion next spring.

glosses: Having the property of soundness.

examples.text: With fresh material, taxonomic conclusions are leavened by recognition that the material examined reflects the site it occupied; a herbarium packet gives one only a small fraction of the data desirable for sound conclusions. Herbarium material does not, indeed, allow one to extrapolate safely: what you see is what you get[…]

glosses: Good; acceptable; decent.

examples.text: How are you? —I'm sound.
That's a sound track you're playing.
See that man over there? He's sound. You should get to know him.

glosses: Quiet and deep.

examples.text: Sound asleep means sleeping peacefully, and often deeply.
Her sleep was sound.

glosses: Heavy; laid on with force.

examples.text: a sound beating

glosses: Founded in law; legal; valid; not defective.

examples.text: a sound title to land

glosses: Soundly.

examples.text: So ſound he ſlept, that nought mought him awake.

glosses: Yes; used to show agreement or understanding.

examples.text: I found my jacket. — Sound.

glosses: A sensation perceived by the ear caused by the vibration of air or some other medium.

examples.text: He turned when he heard the sound of footsteps behind him.  Nobody made a sound.
The warlike sound / Of trumpets loud and clarions.
Through all the Worlds are sounds, the noises of moving, and the echoes of voices and song; but upon the River is no sound ever heard, for there all echoes die.

glosses: A vibration capable of causing such sensations.

examples.text: In trumpets for assisting the hearing, all reverbation of the trumpet must be avoided. It must be made thick, of the least elastic materials, and covered with cloth externally. For all reverbation lasts for a short time, and produces new sounds which mix with those which are coming in.

It was April 22, 1831, and a young man was walking down Whitehall in the direction of Parliament Street.[…]. He halted opposite the Privy Gardens, and, with his face turned skywards, listened until the sound of the Tower guns smote again on the ear and dispelled his doubts.

glosses: A distinctive style and sonority of a particular musician, orchestra etc.

examples.text: He looks like he's got it, maybe. Listen to those kids!/There's no maybe about it. That's it, that's the sound.

glosses: Noise without meaning; empty noise.

examples.text: For let us conſider this Prepoſition as to its meaning, (for it is the ſence, and not ſound, that is and muſt be the Principle or common Notion) […]

glosses: Earshot, distance within which a certain noise may be heard.

examples.text: Stay within the sound of my voice.

glosses: A segment as a part of spoken language, the smallest unit of spoken language, a speech sound.
To produce a sound.

examples.text: When the horn sounds, take cover.

glosses: To convey an impression by one's sound.

examples.text: He sounded good when we last spoke.
That story sounds like a pack of lies!
How silver-sweet sound lovers' tongues!

glosses: To be conveyed in sound; to be spread or published; to convey intelligence by sound.

examples.text: For from you ſounded out the worde of the Lord, not in Macedonia & in Achaia onely: but your faith alſo which is towarde God, ſpred abroade in all quarters, that we nede not to ſpeake any thing.

glosses: To resound.
To arise or to be recognizable as arising in or from a particular area of law, or as likely to result in a particular kind of legal remedy.

examples.text: In my opinion this claim sounds in damages rather than in an injunction.
[…]there can be no doubt that claims brought pursuant to § 1983 sound in tort.

glosses: To cause to produce a sound.

examples.text: Sound the alarm!
He sounds the instrument.

If a train enters the forward section before its description has been transmitted, a "not described" lamp is illuminated on the transmitter, an alarm buzzer is sounded, and the lamp remains alight until a description has been transmitted.

glosses: To pronounce.

examples.text: The "e" in "house" isn't sounded.

glosses: A long narrow inlet, or a strait between the mainland and an island; also, a strait connecting two seas, or connecting a sea or lake with the ocean.

examples.text: Puget Sound; Owen Sound; Long Island Sound
The Sound of Denmarke, where ships pay toll.

glosses: The air bladder of a fish.

examples.text: Cod sounds are an esteemed article of food.
The head was chopped off, the belly opened, the liver set aside--sometimes along with the roe, sounds, throats, and other items.

glosses: Of a whale, to dive downwards.

examples.text: The whale sounded and eight hundred feet of heavy line streaked out of the line tub before he ended his dive.

glosses: To ascertain, or to try to ascertain, the thoughts, motives, and purposes of (a person); to examine; to try; to test; to probe.

examples.text: When I sounded him, he appeared to favor the proposed deal.
Tell me moreouer, haſt thou ſounded him,/If he appeale the Duke on ancient malice,/Or worthily as a good ſubiect ſhould/On ſome knowne ground of treacherie in him.
I was in Jeſt: / And by that offer meant to ſound your breaſt.
I've sounded my Numidians man by man.

glosses: To fathom or test; to ascertain the depth of water with a sounding line or other device.

examples.text: Mariners on sailing ships would sound the depth of the water with a weighted rope.
As when the Sea-man […]/All fearefull foldes his ſailes, and ſounds the maine,/Lifting his prayers to the heauens for aid,/Againſt the terrour of the winds and waues.

glosses: To examine with the instrument called a sound or sonde, or by auscultation or percussion.

examples.text: to sound a patient, or the bladder or urethra

glosses: A long, thin probe for sounding or dilating body cavities or canals such as the urethra; a sonde.

examples.text: Most mild cases respond very nicely to such relatively simple office procedures as dilatations with sounds of increasing calibre, followed by the instillation of an ounce of 5 per cent argyrol in the bladder.

examples.text: Ayant franchi quelques glaces serrées, nous gagnâmes un chenal d'eau libre le long de terre où nous draguâmes, sondâmes et recueillîmes des températures et échantillons d'eau de mer.

Le soir la vigie signale à quelques encablures de la côte une goélette immobile qui semble donner de la bande. […]. Comme le schooner peut avoir besoin de secours, nous approchons en sondant prudemment.

glosses: Enfoncer, introduire dans certaines choses un instrument fait exprès, pour en connaître la nature ou la qualité.

examples.text: Sonder un terrain, une poutre.
Il s’approchait du canapé et, méthodiquement, sans se hâter, avec une habileté parfaite, il entreprenait de sonder le capitonnage du meuble.

glosses: Tâcher de connaître s’il n’y a pas de danger dans une affaire et de savoir comment il faudra s’y prendre pour réussir.

examples.text: Sonder le terrain,

glosses: Explorer une plaie ou une cavité du corps à l’aide d’une sonde.

examples.text: […] Marguerite, d’une aiguille d’or à la pointe arrondie, sondait les plaies avec toute la délicatesse et l’habileté que maître Ambroise Paré eût pu déployer en pareille circonstance.

glosses: Chercher à connaître.

examples.text: Sonder les dispositions, les intentions de quelqu’un.
Peu à peu elle parvint à ressaisir sa volonté et à se reconnaître. La lumière qu’elle porta alors dans sa situation lui en fit sonder l’horreur dans toute son étendue.

glosses: Chercher à connaître les pensées, les volontés de quelqu’un.

examples.text: Sylvie alla sonder sa conscience au fond du confessionnal.
Il sonda malicieusement ce caractère propre à se courber aux exigences d’un plan pourvu qu’il y trouvât sa pâture.

Pour sonder son frère, Aristide, qui n’osait paraître inquiet ouvertement, se contenta de lui demander :
— As-tu lu mon article d’hier ? Qu’en penses-tu ?

glosses: Plonger, en parlant des baleines, cachalots et autres grands cétacés.

examples.text: Dès qu’elle est harponnée, la baleine sonde avec une vitesse de quinze à dix-sept nœuds, entraînant à sa suite la frêle embarcation et les hommes qui doivent lui donner la mort.
- Je dis que si c’est une baleine, elle sonde, Sir. C’est le terme exact employé sur tous les bateaux de pêche, quand un de ces animaux décide de visiter les profondeurs de l’océan.
